facts.text: Toronto police announced 82 charges against seven accused on Oct. 14, 2026 in probe that began with July 25 abduction
Police allege the victim was abducted at gunpoint near Finch Ave. E. and Bayview Ave., handcuffed and assaulted
Police allege suspects tried to access the victim's cryptocurrency assets and business security systems
Victim was released, threatened and warned not to contact police; minor injuries, has recovered
Talarambage Fernando, 22, James Moreau, 29, and Jack Miley, 24, are 7th Toronto Regiment reservists
Fernando and Moreau arrested Aug. 11; Miley Sept. 24
DND removed the three from duties and restricted access pending administrative review
Police allege ~2,500 rounds and five over-capacity magazines were stolen from the CAF and not reported stolen
Seizures included a shotgun, two 3D-printed handguns, two silencers and 2,700+ rounds
No link to a larger organized crime group has been established
Victim's identity has not been made public
Miley faces seven charges incl. kidnapping for ransom with a firearm; Fernando faces 20 counts
Miley is a master bombardier deployed on Op Reassurance 2025; Fernando enrolled Jan 2020; Moreau enrolled March 2018, Op Laser 2020
Police allege the victim owned a cryptocurrency exchange and was targeted for it
Seizures also included methamphetamine, cocaine, GPS trackers, radios, handcuffs and a balaclava
Global News reports Fernando and Moreau together face 49 charges
No revised charge total below 82 appears in police material or reporting

missed.text: Two suspects were arrested within 24 hours; all seven accused were in custody by Sept. 24
Fernando and Moreau hold the rank of bombardier; DND spokesperson Andree-Anne Poulin confirmed their enrolment
Fernando enrolled January 2020 and never deployed; Moreau enrolled March 2018 and deployed on Operation Laser in 2020
Military police are investigating alongside Toronto police
Charges include kidnapping for ransom and forcible confinement; Moreau alone faces two counts of drug possession for trafficking; Fernando faces 20 of the 82 charges
Seizures included a third 9mm police allege was not safely stored and ten over-capacity magazines; about half the stolen rounds were blanks
Other items recovered: cellphones, replica firearm, knives, hatchets, baton, money counter and Canadian currency
Chief Supt. Joe Matthews said the victim suffered minor injuries and has recovered
DND's earlier statement had suggested organized crime involvement; investigators still reviewing cellphones
DND's emailed statement came Oct. 14; no separate DND news release on the case
